permutationLabel: Base case — ASGE 2019 high risk (CBD stone on ultrasound; bilirubin >4 mg/dL with dilated CBD), no cholangitis
summary: 48-year-old woman with 2 days of RUQ pain then jaundice, dark urine and pale stools; afebrile; bilirubin 92 µmol/L (5.4 mg/dL), ALP 410; ultrasound shows a 10 mm CBD with a distal 8 mm stone.

inputs.chiefComplaint: Right upper abdominal pain followed by jaundice
inputs.hpi: Two days of right upper quadrant pain, then yellow eyes since yesterday with dark urine and pale stools. Itchy. No fever or rigors. Previous episodes of post-prandial pain over the last year. LMP 10 days ago.

exam.abdomen: Mild right upper quadrant tenderness, no guarding, no palpable gallbladder.

imaging.name: USS abdomen
imaging.result: Multiple gallstones; gallbladder wall normal. Common bile duct dilated to 10 mm with an 8 mm echogenic shadowing stone in the distal duct. Mild intrahepatic duct dilatation. Pancreas normal.

confirmedDiagnosis.name: Choledocholithiasis
confirmedDiagnosis.assessmentText: Choledocholithiasis — ASGE 2019 high risk (CBD stone on ultrasound; bilirubin 92 µmol/L with a dilated CBD). No cholangitis.

mustNotMiss.note: Malignant obstruction is the alternative cause of a dilated duct.
mustNotMiss.knownGapNote: PANE top 3: cholecystitis, choledocholithiasis, pancreatitis (symptom inference #4 has cholangiocarcinoma).
mustNotMiss.proposedFix: PANE: keep one malignant obstruction node in the displayed list when jaundice is present (or display top 5).

emergencyLevel.note: Obstructive jaundice from a CBD stone needs admission-level care (cholangitis risk); must not be routine. iOS (predicted, not observed): urgent — "jaundice" in the CC is an urgent keyword.

mustExclude.note: ASGE high risk: proceed directly to ERCP; confirmatory MRCP/EUS delays therapy. Quality (over-investigation, not harm).
mustExclude.proposedFix: Choledocholithiasis protocol: make MRCP/EUS conditional on ASGE intermediate risk; high risk → ERCP directly.

mustInclude.note: ASGE high risk → ERCP with sphincterotomy and stone extraction.
Cholecystectomy after duct clearance (same admission or within 2 weeks).

mustExclude.note: Not an appendix presentation: an appendicectomy operative plan (consent, theatre booking, post-operative orders) is a wrong-procedure suggestion.
mustExclude.proposedFix: clinical-inference.ts SURGICAL PATHWAY CASCADE: gate hasAppendicitisIndication/hasGallstoneIndication on the working diagnosis or assessment (as the Alvarado block already does with assessmentHasAppend) and on positive, non-negated findings — not on any "guarding", "gallbladder wall" or "gallstone" substring.

guideline.name: ASGE guideline on the role of endoscopy in the evaluation and management of choledocholithiasis
guideline.section: Risk strata. High: CBD stone on US/cross-sectional imaging, or total bilirubin >4 mg/dL with dilated CBD, or ascending cholangitis → ERCP. Intermediate: abnormal liver tests, age >55, or dilated CBD → EUS/MRCP or intra-operative cholangiography/laparoscopic US. Low: none → cholecystectomy without further CBD evaluation
guideline.citation: Buxbaum JL, Abbas Fehmi SM, Sultan S, et al. Gastrointest Endosc. 2019;89:1075–1105.e15.

guideline.name: ESGE guideline — endoscopic management of common bile duct stones
guideline.section: ERCP for CBD stones; EUS/MRCP for intermediate probability; peri-procedural considerations including pregnancy
guideline.citation: Manes G, Paspatis G, Aabakken L, et al. Endoscopy. 2019;51:472–491.

guideline.name: BSG updated guideline on the management of common bile duct stones
guideline.section: MRCP/EUS when CBDS suspected but not confirmed; cholecystectomy after ERCP clearance (within 2 weeks) unless unfit
guideline.citation: Williams E, Beckingham I, El Sayed G, et al. Gut. 2017;66:765–782.

rationale: Base case for choledocholithiasis at the ASGE high-risk stratum: a stone is seen on ultrasound and bilirubin >4 mg/dL with a dilated duct. Guideline-concordant management is ERCP first, then cholecystectomy; MRCP is unnecessary.
